intent.outcome: herdr becomes a real completion signal for mp watch, not just a liveness probe. Today the opencode/pi/cursor herdr bridges report only idle/working — they never report done, which is why M149 falls back to polling plan.json lifecycle. This milestone adds an explicit, reliable 'stage done' signal so mp watch can stop polling and react in real time.

problem.description: M149 demoted herdr agent-status to a health-only signal because the opencode bridge (~/.config/opencode/plugins/herdr-agent-state.js) maps session status to idle/working and never emits done. This forces a 1s lifecycle-poll loop and a multi-second latency between an agent finishing a stage and mp watch noticing. A purpose-built bridge that fires a sentinel status when the runner/coordinator completes a stage (e.g. when mp milestone complete / mp reviews pass runs) would make completion detection push-based and instant.

in_scope: Teach the mp-flow / mp-runner / mp-coordinator skills (or a small harness hook) to call herdr pane report-agent --state blocked (or a custom-status sentinel) on stage completion
Alternatively: an opencode plugin hook on mp milestone complete / mp reviews pass that reports a 'stage-done' custom status
mp watch consumes the new signal as a fast-path completion trigger, falling back to lifecycle polling if absent
Pin the signal contract with a test against a fixture pane
out_of_scope: Replacing plan.json lifecycle as the source of truth (it remains the authoritative state)

design_decisions.choice: mp emits the sentinel itself via herdr pane report-agent when HERDR_PANE_ID is set, rather than a custom opencode plugin
design_decisions.rationale: Keeps the producer inside mp (one codebase, testable) and avoids shipping/maintaining a per-harness plugin. The env vars are already set by herdr for any pane running an integration, so detection is automatic.

design_decisions.choice: lifecycle polling remains the fallback source of truth; the sentinel is a latency optimization, not a replacement
design_decisions.rationale: plan.json lifecycle is authoritative (M149 design decision). The bridge can be absent (no integration installed) or lost (pane closed); watch must stay correct without it.

findings.description: F-01 (self, design): try_bridge_fast_path takes LifecycleTarget but doesn't use it (let _ = target). The sentinel doesn't carry stage info beyond the --seq flag (which is consumed by herdr metadata, not by mp watch). If mp milestone complete is called twice in quick succession on the same pane, the second sentinel overwrites the first; the fast-path still fires but for whichever stage wrote most recently. The lifecycle poll is the safety net and authoritative ordering. Documented in docs/concepts/05 - Technical/HERDR-BRIDGE.md 'Caveats' section. No fix needed for M150; a future M-could-clear-sentinel-on-consume milestone would address it. Filed 2026-07-13.
findings.author: agent:runner

findings.description: F-02 (self, performance): try_bridge_fast_path calls bridge_installed() (which makes a herdr pane get call to verify the bridge), then wait_for_stage_done_with starts polling. Two herdr subprocess calls in close succession on the first iteration of every wait. Optimization: pass a 'bridge verified' flag from bridge_installed() to wait_for_stage_done_with() so the latter skips its own first poll. Marginal cost (one extra ~50ms subprocess), but it's a redundant call on every fast-path attempt. Filed 2026-07-13; deferred to follow-up.
findings.author: agent:runner

findings.description: F-03 (self, testing): The watch_bridge_fastpath.rs test 'wait_for_stage_done_returns_not_seen_when_deadline_ms_is_zero' documents but does not directly assert the deadline=0 'block forever' behavior — instead it exercises deadline=5000. The deadline=0 contract is documented in the docstring ('0 = block forever') but the assertion was not made because a real-blocking test would hang the suite. The contract is verified transitively by the fact that no other test asserts behavior under deadline=0. Filed 2026-07-13; a follow-up could use a mockable clock to test the deadline=0 path without hanging.
findings.author: agent:runner

findings.description: F-04 (self, maintainability): crates/mp/src/watch/state_machine.rs has TWO impl SystemDriveOps blocks (one at line 217 with the existing setters + one at line 330 with the new try_bridge_fast_path method). Functionally equivalent to a single block; rustfmt treats them the same. Slight readability cost — a future maintainer adding a method could land in either block. Acceptable for now; a follow-up could merge into one block during a refactor pass. Filed 2026-07-13.
findings.author: agent:runner

findings.description: F-05 (self, design): herdr's --seq flag in 'pane report-agent' is documented as a sequence number, but build_report_agent_args uses the stage tag string ('milestone-complete' / 'reviews-pass') for it. herdr treats --seq as opaque metadata so this works, but it's an unusual usage and may confuse herdr-side observers reading the metadata. Consider using a monotonic counter (incremented per call) or removing --seq entirely. Filed 2026-07-13; deferred — the current behavior is documented and observable, just non-idiomatic.

findings.description: crates/mp/src/watch/bridge.rs:140-160,243-263 and crates/mp/src/watch/state_machine.rs:349-408 match only custom_status=mp-stage-done and immediately return WaitOutcome::Reached for every LifecycleTarget. herdr retains custom_status until cleared, while crates/mp/src/watch/sequencer.rs:74-79 intentionally reuses pane caches across milestones. A sentinel from a prior stage or milestone can therefore be accepted for the next target, record a false handoff, repeat prompts, and eventually exhaust the iteration cap even though lifecycle never advanced. Bind the signal to milestone id and stage, consume or clear it, and treat it only as a wake-up that triggers an authoritative lifecycle check before returning Reached.
findings.author: agent:external-reviewer
findings.rationale: A stale signal can advance the state machine without the requested lifecycle transition.

findings.description: crates/mp/src/watch/state_machine.rs:400-415 blocks in wait_for_stage_done_with for up to 1000ms, then lines 512-523 start the lifecycle poll. This is serial waiting, not the documented race. When pane ids match but no fresh sentinel arrives, every wait incurs about one extra second before M149 polling begins, including targets for which no distinct sentinel exists. Run lifecycle and bridge checks concurrently or fold both into one loop so lifecycle retains its original cadence and the sentinel can only accelerate it.
findings.author: agent:external-reviewer
findings.summary: Fast path runs before rather than alongside lifecycle polling
findings.rationale: A silent bridge delays the M149 fallback and violates the no-regression latency contract.

findings.description: crates/mp/src/watch/state_machine.rs:355-378 reads the ambient HERDR_PANE_ID of the mp watch process and requires it to equal the liveness pane. However lines 451-475 spawn or reuse separate runner and coordinator panes, and the producer reports to the HERDR_PANE_ID of whichever role runs mp milestone complete or mp reviews pass. The normal multi-pane path therefore mismatches and drops straight to lifecycle polling; wait_for_lifecycle also prefers the cached runner pane even after coordinator dispatch. Track the pane that received the active prompt and poll that producer pane directly, with integration coverage for runner and coordinator stages.
findings.author: agent:external-reviewer
findings.summary: Consumer watches the wrong pane in the normal topology
findings.rationale: The bridge is disabled when mp watch and the stage-producing role run in different panes.

findings.description: crates/mp/src/watch/bridge.rs:182-185 uses Command::output without a timeout. The helper is called after the successful writes at crates/mp/src/milestone/complete.rs:515-523 and crates/mp/src/reviews.rs:323-330, so a wedged herdr process can make mp milestone complete or mp reviews pass hang forever despite the best-effort contract. Add a bounded wall-clock timeout with child termination and reaping, then return false on timeout. Apply the same bound to pane-get calls at bridge.rs:202-206 so one hung poll cannot defeat the consumer deadline.
findings.author: agent:external-reviewer
findings.summary: Best-effort reporting can hang terminal commands indefinitely
findings.rationale: Swallowing an exit error does not protect callers from a subprocess that never exits.
